title: VideoGameQA-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models for Video Game Quality Assurance
key_findings: Standard zero-shot VLMs detect coarse bugs (~78% accuracy) but fail severely on micro-clipping and precise bounding boxes, frequently hallucinating on stylized art.
primary_limitations: High inference latency (>1.5s/frame); poor spatial bounding localization for subtle geometry defects.

title: A Hybrid Co-Finetuning Approach for Visual Bug Detection in Video Games
key_findings: Co-finetuning leveraging labelled target frames, co-domain games, and unlabelled gameplay frames boosts recall by +18.4% mAP without manual exhaustive labels.
primary_limitations: Significant cross-domain degradation when transferring across radically divergent art styles (e.g. realistic 3D to voxel).

title: State-Aware Visual Glitch Detection in Complex 3D Video Games Using Deep Multimodal Representations
key_findings: Fusing game-engine internal telemetry (transform matrices and collision queries) with RGB vision reduces false positives by 42% compared to pure vision.
primary_limitations: Requires engine-level instrumentation hooks; cannot be deployed as a black-box tester on closed commercial builds.

title: How Far Can VLMs Go for Visual Bug Detection? Studying 19738 Keyframes from 41 Hours of Gameplay Videos
key_findings: Baseline VLM achieves 0.50 precision and 0.72 accuracy; secondary judge models and report-retrieval prompting provide only marginal gains while inflating compute cost.
primary_limitations: Low temporal sensitivity; prompt sensitivity; prone to mistaking intentional stylized art for visual defects.

title: RefGlitch-Bench: A Benchmark for Reference-based Gameplay Glitch Detection with Vision-Language Models
authors: Yu, Wiens, Barahona-Rios, Wilkins, Zadtootaghaj, Barman, Bezemer
key_findings: Formulating glitch detection as an explicit within-video comparison with a reference frame (Last Clean Frame) dramatically reduces false alarms and resolves ambiguity.
primary_limitations: Requires reliable reference frame selection; error propagation occurs when the selected reference frame itself contains subtle artifacts.

title: TempGlitch: Detecting Temporal Visual Glitches in Continuous Gameplay Video Streams
key_findings: Single-frame anomaly detectors miss over 65% of animation and flickering glitches; sliding-window temporal attention over 16-frame buffers is essential for streaming playtests.
primary_limitations: High computational footprint; current video transformer backbones are too heavy for 60 FPS real-time CI playtesting.

title: Weak Supervision for Label Efficient Visual Bug Detection in Video Games
key_findings: Domain-specific weak supervision with just 5 clean exemplar frames improves F1 score from 0.336 to 0.550 in low-prevalence first-person player clipping regimes.
primary_limitations: Evaluated primarily on first-person clipping in a single open-world game; generalisation to other glitch classes unverified.

title: Automatically Detecting Visual Bugs in HTML5 Canvas Games
key_findings: Internal canvas decomposition and oracle sprite comparison achieves 100% accuracy on injected canvas bugs vs 44.6% for naive screenshot diffing.
primary_limitations: Restricted to 2D web canvas games with static sprites; inapplicable to dynamic 3D lighting and complex vertex shaders.

title: Video Game Automated Testing Approaches: An Assessment Framework
key_findings: Comprehensive framework categorizing game testing techniques; establishes visual regression as the least automated and most vulnerable testing sector.
primary_limitations: Taxonomic review without deep learning implementation or empirical CV benchmark.

title: A Literature Review of Software Testing Practices and Frameworks in the Video Gaming Industry
key_findings: Reveals that while game logic unit tests are automating rapidly, visual QA remains over 80% manual in industry due to brittle computer vision tooling.
primary_limitations: General software engineering scope; lacks technical algorithmic analysis of modern CV/VLM architectures.
